newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's floods hit 20,000 hectares of crops.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's floods hit 20,000 hectares of crops.

text.p: Morocco said on Tuesday exceptional winter rainfall has flooded nearly 20,000 hectares (50,000 acres) of farmland.
"According to the first estimates, floods have hit nearly 20,000 hectares of cereals and sugar crops, mainly in the Ghrab and Loukkos regions," an official at the agriculture ministry told Reuters.
The rich farming Gharb and Loukkos areas are located in the north of Morocco.
Two thousand hectares (5,000 acres) of cane and sugar beet were submerged by waters in the two northern regions, the official added.
A preliminary report on the situation of crops was expected to be published in the coming weeks, he said.

Asked about the impact of floods on the country's cereal imports, an official at the state-owned Office Interprofessionnel des Cereales et Legumineuses said: "At this stage we do not expect the floods to have an impact on our scheduled imports."
Morocco plans to import 1.0 million tonnes of soft wheat in 1996/97 season starting from last July, officials said.
Morocco last year harvested a record of 9.75 million tonnes of cereals and a total of 76,800 hectares (192,000 acres) of sugar cane and beet, the ministry said.

Abdslam Chaachou, head of the Casablanca meteorological centre, told Reuters on Tuesday: "Some Moroccan agricultural areas including the Gharb area received more than double the quantity of rains in December compared with the same period in 1995."

During parliamentary debates, Interior Minister Driss Basri told the 333-seat house of representatives that "the heavy rains which hit our country did not result in a catastrophic situation as some people say."
According to the agriculture ministry, 5.6 million hectares (14 million acres) are expected to be sown for all crops in the 1996/97 season, similar to the area for 1995/96.
Nearly 900,000 hectares (2,250,000 acres) are located in irrigated areas, it added.
